lesson_scope: Position vectors in 3D, displacement vectors, magnitude, unit vectors, midpoints, ratio divisions, and geometric models in prisms, pyramids, and tetrahedra.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: 3D displacement vector from two points.

walkthrough.text:
Recall the definition of the displacement vector $\vec{AB}$ from initial point $A$ to terminal point $B$:
$$\vec{AB} = \vec{OB} - \vec{OA}$$

Substitute the given position vectors $\vec{OA} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -1 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}$ and $\vec{OB} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 3 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}$:
$$\vec{AB} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 3 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -1 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}$$

Subtract corresponding components to find the resulting column vector:
$$x = 5 - 2 = 3$$
$$y = 3 - (-1) = 3 + 1 = 4$$
$$z = -2 - 4 = -6$$
$$\vec{AB} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \\ -6 \end{pmatrix}$$

State the 3D magnitude formula for a vector $\mathbf{v} = v_1\mathbf{i} + v_2\mathbf{j} + v_3\mathbf{k}$:
$$|\mathbf{v}| = \sqrt{v_1^2 + v_2^2 + v_3^2}$$

Substitute the given components $v_1 = 2$, $v_2 = -3$, and $v_3 = 6$ into the formula:
$$|\mathbf{v}| = \sqrt{2^2 + (-3)^2 + 6^2} = \sqrt{4 + 9 + 36}$$

Simplify the sum under the square root:
$$|\mathbf{v}| = \sqrt{49} = 7$$

State the definition of the unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{a}}$ in the direction of vector $\mathbf{a}$:
$$\hat{\mathbf{a}} = \frac{1}{|\mathbf{a}|} \mathbf{a}$$

Calculate the magnitude of $\mathbf{a} = 4\mathbf{i} - 2\mathbf{j} + 4\mathbf{k}$:
$$|\mathbf{a}| = \sqrt{4^2 + (-2)^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{16 + 4 + 16} = \sqrt{36} = 6$$

Divide each component of $\mathbf{a}$ by its magnitude $|\mathbf{a}| = 6$ and simplify fractions:
$$\hat{\mathbf{a}} = \frac{1}{6}(4\mathbf{i} - 2\mathbf{j} + 4\mathbf{k}) = \frac{4}{6}\mathbf{i} - \frac{2}{6}\mathbf{j} + \frac{4}{6}\mathbf{k} = \frac{2}{3}\mathbf{i} - \frac{1}{3}\mathbf{j} + \frac{2}{3}\mathbf{k}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: 3D midpoint vector and origin distance.

walkthrough.text:
Apply the midpoint position vector formula for points $P$ and $Q$:
$$\vec{OM} = \frac{1}{2}(\mathbf{p} + \mathbf{q})$$

Substitute $\mathbf{p} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 4 \\ -3 \end{pmatrix}$ and $\mathbf{q} = \begin{pmatrix} 7 \\ -2 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix}$:
$$\vec{OM} = \frac{1}{2}\left( \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 4 \\ -3 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} 7 \\ -2 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix} \right) = \frac{1}{2} \begin{pmatrix} 1 + 7 \\ 4 + (-2) \\ -3 + 5 \end{pmatrix} = \frac{1}{2} \begin{pmatrix} 8 \\ 2 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$$

Calculate the exact distance $OM = |\vec{OM}|$ using the 3D magnitude formula:
$$OM = \sqrt{4^2 + 1^2 + 1^2} = \sqrt{16 + 1 + 1} = \sqrt{18} = 3\sqrt{2}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Ratio division of a line segment.

walkthrough.text:
Apply the section formula for internal division. Since $AC : CB = 1 : 2$, point $C$ divides $AB$ in the ratio $1 : 2$:
$$\vec{OC} = \vec{OA} + \frac{1}{1 + 2}\vec{AB} = \frac{2\vec{OA} + \vec{OB}}{3}$$

Substitute $\vec{OA} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$ and $\vec{OB} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ -1 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix}$:
$$\vec{OC} = \frac{1}{3}\left( 2\begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ -1 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix} \right) = \frac{1}{3}\left( \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 4 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ -1 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix} \right)$$

Sum the components and divide by 3 to obtain the position vector and coordinates:
$$\vec{OC} = \frac{1}{3}\begin{pmatrix} 2 + 4 \\ 4 + (-1) \\ -2 + 5 \end{pmatrix} = \frac{1}{3}\begin{pmatrix} 6 \\ 3 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$$
$$\text{Coordinates of } C = (2, 1, 1)$$

hints: In the base rectangle $OABC$, $B$ has the $x$-coordinate of $A$ and the $y$-coordinate of $C$: $B(4, 6, 0)$.
$F$ is vertically above $B$ by 5 units, so $z = 5$: $F(4, 6, 5)$.

walkthrough.text:
Determine coordinates of base vertex $B$. In the rectangular base $OABC$ in the $xy$-plane ($z = 0$) with $O(0, 0, 0)$, $A(4, 0, 0)$, and $C(0, 6, 0)$, vertex $B$ is located opposite origin $O$:
$$\vec{OB} = \vec{OA} + \vec{OC} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 6 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 6 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} \implies B(4, 6, 0)$$

Determine coordinates of upper vertex $F$. Vertex $F$ lies vertically above $B$ parallel to the $z$-axis at height 5:
$$\vec{OF} = \vec{OB} + 5\mathbf{k} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 6 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 6 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix} \implies F(4, 6, 5)$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Core: rectangular prism position vectors, edge midpoints, and segment lengths.

walkthrough.text:
Find the position vector of vertex $F$. In the cuboid, $F$ is diagonally opposite to origin $O$ along all three coordinate axes ($x = 6, y = 4, z = 3$):
$$\vec{OF} = \vec{OA} + \vec{OC} + \vec{OD} = \begin{pmatrix} 6 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 4 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 6 \\ 4 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$$

Find the position vectors of vertices $B$ and $G$. Point $B$ is in the $xy$-plane at $(6, 4, 0)$ and point $G$ is in the $yz$-plane at $(0, 4, 3)$:
$$\vec{OB} = \begin{pmatrix} 6 \\ 4 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}, \quad \vec{OG} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 4 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$$

Compute the midpoint $M$ of edge $BG$ using the midpoint formula:
$$\vec{OM} = \frac{1}{2}(\vec{OB} + \vec{OG}) = \frac{1}{2}\left( \begin{pmatrix} 6 \\ 4 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 4 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} \right) = \frac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix} 6 \\ 8 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \\ 1.5 \end{pmatrix}$$

Find the displacement vector $\vec{AM}$ using vector subtraction $\vec{AM} = \vec{OM} - \vec{OA}$:
$$\vec{AM} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \\ 1.5 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 6 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 - 6 \\ 4 - 0 \\ 1.5 - 0 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -3 \\ 4 \\ 1.5 \end{pmatrix}$$

Calculate the magnitude $|\vec{AM}|$ using the 3D distance formula:
$$|\vec{AM}| = \sqrt{(-3)^2 + 4^2 + (1.5)^2} = \sqrt{9 + 16 + 2.25} = \sqrt{27.25}$$

Convert $27.25$ into an exact simplified fraction in surd form:
$$27.25 = \frac{109}{4} \implies AM = \sqrt{\frac{109}{4}} = \frac{\sqrt{109}}{2}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Core: 3D pyramid apex and base coordinate geometry with ratio point division.

walkthrough.text:
State the position vectors of apex $V$ and base vertex $A$:
$$\mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{a} = \begin{pmatrix} -2 \\ -3 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}$$

Calculate the displacement vector $\vec{VA} = \mathbf{a} - \mathbf{v}$:
$$\vec{VA} = \begin{pmatrix} -2 \\ -3 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -2 \\ -3 \\ -6 \end{pmatrix}$$

Compute the magnitude of $\vec{VA}$ to show the length of the sloping edge is 7:
$$|\vec{VA}| = \sqrt{(-2)^2 + (-3)^2 + (-6)^2} = \sqrt{4 + 9 + 36} = \sqrt{49} = 7$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Point on sloping edge with ratio.

hints: Since $VP : PA = 2 : 1$, $P$ is $\frac{2}{3}$ of the way along $\vec{VA}$ from $V$.

walkthrough.text:
Use the ratio $VP : PA = 2 : 1$. The total parts along $VA$ are $2 + 1 = 3$. Therefore, $P$ is located $\frac{2}{3}$ of the distance from $V$ towards $A$:
$$\vec{OP} = \vec{OV} + \frac{2}{3}\vec{VA}$$

Substitute $\vec{OV} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix}$ and $\vec{VA} = \begin{pmatrix} -2 \\ -3 \\ -6 \end{pmatrix}$:
$$\vec{OP} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix} + \frac{2}{3}\begin{pmatrix} -2 \\ -3 \\ -6 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} -\frac{4}{3} \\ -2 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix}$$

Add corresponding components to obtain the position vector of $P$:
$$\vec{OP} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 - \frac{4}{3} \\ 0 - 2 \\ 6 - 4 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -\frac{4}{3} \\ -2 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Core: 3D parallelogram vector algebra and diagonal length computation.

hints: Add components: $\begin{pmatrix} 2 + 4 - 5 \\ 3 + p - (-1) \\ -1 + q - 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ p + 4 \\ q - 4 \end{pmatrix}$.

walkthrough.text: Apply the vector condition for a parallelogram: opposite directed sides are equal vectors, so $\vec{AB} = \vec{DC}$.

Express in terms of position vectors and rearrange to isolate $\mathbf{d}$:
$$\mathbf{b} - \mathbf{a} = \mathbf{c} - \mathbf{d} \implies \mathbf{d} = \mathbf{a} + \mathbf{c} - \mathbf{b}$$

Substitute $\mathbf{a} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$, $\mathbf{b} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ -1 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$, and $\mathbf{c} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ p \\ q \end{pmatrix}$:
$$\mathbf{d} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ p \\ q \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ -1 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 + 4 - 5 \\ 3 + p - (-1) \\ -1 + q - 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ p + 4 \\ q - 4 \end{pmatrix}$$

hints: Equate components to $(1, 1, 2)$: $p + 4 = 1 \implies p = -3$, and $q - 4 = 2 \implies q = 6$.

walkthrough.text:
Equate the expression for $\mathbf{d}$ with the given coordinates of $D(1, 1, 2)$:
$$\begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ p + 4 \\ q - 4 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$$

Solve the scalar equations for $p$ and $q$:
$$p + 4 = 1 \implies p = 1 - 4 = -3$$
$$q - 4 = 2 \implies q = 2 + 4 = 6$$

With $p = -3$ and $q = 6$, vertex $C$ is $(4, -3, 6)$. Find the displacement vector $\vec{AC} = \mathbf{c} - \mathbf{a}$:
$$\vec{AC} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ -3 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 - 2 \\ -3 - 3 \\ 6 - (-1) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -6 \\ 7 \end{pmatrix}$$

Calculate the exact length of diagonal $AC$:
$$|\vec{AC}| = \sqrt{2^2 + (-6)^2 + 7^2} = \sqrt{4 + 36 + 49} = \sqrt{89}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Core: triangular prism centroid deduction and diagonal midpoint calculation.

hints: Centroid of a triangle is the arithmetic mean of its three vertices: $\mathbf{g} = \frac{\mathbf{v}_1 + \mathbf{v}_2 + \mathbf{v}_3}{3}$.

walkthrough.text:
State the centroid formula for a triangle with vertices having position vectors $\mathbf{u}_1, \mathbf{u}_2, \mathbf{u}_3$:
$$\vec{OG} = \frac{1}{3}(\mathbf{u}_1 + \mathbf{u}_2 + \mathbf{u}_3)$$

Compute the centroid $G_1$ of base triangle $OAB$ with $O(0,0,0), A(4,0,0), B(0,3,0)$:
$$\vec{OG_1} = \frac{1}{3}\left( \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 3 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} \right) = \frac{1}{3}\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 3 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 4/3 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}$$

Compute the centroid $G_2$ of top triangle $DEF$ with $D(0,0,5), E(4,0,5), F(0,3,5)$:
$$\vec{OG_2} = \frac{1}{3}\left( \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 0 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 3 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix} \right) = \frac{1}{3}\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 3 \\ 15 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 4/3 \\ 1 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix}$$

hints: $\vec{G_1 G_2} = \vec{OG_2} - \vec{OG_1} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix} = 5\mathbf{k}$, which is parallel to the $z$-axis.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the displacement vector $\vec{G_1 G_2} = \vec{OG_2} - \vec{OG_1}$:
$$\vec{G_1 G_2} = \begin{pmatrix} 4/3 \\ 1 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 4/3 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix} = 5\mathbf{k}$$

Since the $x$-component and $y$-component are both 0, the vector $\vec{G_1 G_2}$ is parallel to the $z$-axis (normal to the horizontal plane $z = 0$), proving that the line segment $G_1 G_2$ is strictly vertical.

Find the midpoint of diagonal $AF$ joining $A(4, 0, 0)$ and $F(0, 3, 5)$:
$$\text{Midpoint} = \frac{1}{2}(\vec{OA} + \vec{OF}) = \frac{1}{2}\left( \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 3 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix} \right) = \frac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 3 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix} = (2, 1.5, 2.5)$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Capstone: regular tetrahedron skew edge midpoint vector proof and exact 3D radical length evaluation.

walkthrough.text:
Express the position vector of midpoint $M$ of edge $OA$ (where $O$ is the origin):
$$\vec{OM} = \frac{1}{2}\vec{OA} = \frac{1}{2}\mathbf{a}$$

Express the position vector of midpoint $N$ of edge $BC$:
$$\vec{ON} = \frac{1}{2}(\vec{OB} + \vec{OC}) = \frac{1}{2}(\mathbf{b} + \mathbf{c})$$

Apply vector subtraction to express the displacement vector $\vec{MN} = \vec{ON} - \vec{OM}$:
$$\vec{MN} = \frac{1}{2}(\mathbf{b} + \mathbf{c}) - \frac{1}{2}\mathbf{a} = \frac{1}{2}(\mathbf{b} + \mathbf{c} - \mathbf{a})$$

Substitute $\mathbf{a} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}$, $\mathbf{b} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ \sqrt{3} \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}$, and $\mathbf{c} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \\ \frac{2\sqrt{6}}{3} \end{pmatrix}$ to find $\mathbf{b} + \mathbf{c} - \mathbf{a}$:
$$\mathbf{b} + \mathbf{c} - \mathbf{a} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ \sqrt{3} \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \\ \frac{2\sqrt{6}}{3} \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 + 1 - 2 \\ \sqrt{3} + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} - 0 \\ 0 + \frac{2\sqrt{6}}{3} - 0 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ \frac{4\sqrt{3}}{3} \\ \frac{2\sqrt{6}}{3} \end{pmatrix}$$

Multiply by $\frac{1}{2}$ to obtain the displacement vector $\vec{MN}$:
$$\vec{MN} = \frac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ \frac{4\sqrt{3}}{3} \\ \frac{2\sqrt{6}}{3} \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ \frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3} \\ \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3} \end{pmatrix}$$

Calculate the square of the magnitude $|\vec{MN}|^2$:
$$|\vec{MN}|^2 = 0^2 + \left(\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}\right)^2 = 0 + \frac{4 \times 3}{9} + \frac{6}{9} = \frac{12 + 6}{9} = \frac{18}{9} = 2$$

Take the square root to determine the exact length:
$$|\vec{MN}| = \sqrt{2}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Capstone: real-world solar panel planar geometry, unit direction vector, diagonal intersection and vertical elevation.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate displacement vectors of opposite sides $\vec{AB}$ and $\vec{DC}$:
$$\vec{AB} = \mathbf{b} - \mathbf{a} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 0 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$$
$$\vec{DC} = \mathbf{c} - \mathbf{d} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 3 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$$
Since $\vec{AB} = \vec{DC}$, the opposite sides are parallel and equal in length, which proves that the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a parallelogram.

Compute the magnitude of edge vector $\vec{AB}$:
$$|\vec{AB}| = \sqrt{4^2 + 0^2 + 1^2} = \sqrt{16 + 0 + 1} = \sqrt{17}$$

Form the unit vector $\hat{\vec{AB}}$ in the direction of $AB$:
$$\hat{\vec{AB}} = \frac{1}{|\vec{AB}|}\vec{AB} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{17}}\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$$

hints: In a parallelogram, diagonals bisect each other at the midpoint of $AC$.
Height above ground $z = 0$ is the $z$-coordinate, which is $3$.

walkthrough.text:
In a parallelogram, the diagonals bisect each other at centre $K$. Calculate the midpoint of diagonal $AC$:
$$\vec{OK} = \frac{1}{2}(\mathbf{a} + \mathbf{c}) = \frac{1}{2}\left( \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 3 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix} \right) = \frac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 3 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1.5 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$$

Verify using diagonal $BD$:
$$\frac{1}{2}(\mathbf{b} + \mathbf{d}) = \frac{1}{2}\left( \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 0 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} \right) = \frac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 3 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1.5 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$$

State the position vector of centre $K$ and its height above the ground plane $z = 0$:
$$\vec{OK} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1.5 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}, \quad \text{Height} = z = 3$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Capstone: parallel vector displacement scaling and exact 3D segment length ratios.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the displacement vector $\vec{QR} = \mathbf{r} - \mathbf{q}$:
$$\vec{QR} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ -2 \\ 7 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 - 5 \\ 4 - (-2) \\ 1 - 7 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -2 \\ 6 \\ -6 \end{pmatrix}$$

Multiply the displacement vector $\vec{QR}$ by scalar 2 to obtain $\vec{PS}$:
$$\vec{PS} = 2\vec{QR} = 2\begin{pmatrix} -2 \\ 6 \\ -6 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -4 \\ 12 \\ -12 \end{pmatrix}$$

Add $\vec{PS}$ to the position vector of $P$ to find the position vector $\mathbf{s} = \vec{OS}$:
$$\mathbf{s} = \mathbf{p} + \vec{PS} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} + \begin{pmatrix} -4 \\ 12 \\ -12 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 - 4 \\ 2 + 12 \\ 3 - 12 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -3 \\ 14 \\ -9 \end{pmatrix}$$

Calculate the displacement vector $\vec{PR} = \mathbf{r} - \mathbf{p}$ and evaluate its exact magnitude:
$$\vec{PR} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 2 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}$$
$$|\vec{PR}| = \sqrt{2^2 + 2^2 + (-2)^2} = \sqrt{4 + 4 + 4} = \sqrt{12} = 2\sqrt{3}$$

Evaluate the exact magnitude of displacement vector $\vec{QR} = \begin{pmatrix} -2 \\ 6 \\ -6 \end{pmatrix}$:
$$|\vec{QR}| = \sqrt{(-2)^2 + 6^2 + (-6)^2} = \sqrt{4 + 36 + 36} = \sqrt{76} = \sqrt{4 \times 19} = 2\sqrt{19}$$

Form the ratio $\frac{|\vec{PR}|}{|\vec{QR}|}$ and simplify the surd by rationalising the denominator:
$$\text{Ratio} = \frac{|\vec{PR}|}{|\vec{QR}|} = \frac{2\sqrt{3}}{2\sqrt{19}} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{19}} = \frac{\sqrt{3}\sqrt{19}}{19} = \frac{\sqrt{57}}{19}$$
